blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Mechanistic linkage between CFTR chloride transport and airway-surface dehydration in cystic fibrosis.
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

evidence_map.claim: CFTR is a membrane chloride channel; chloride transport helps control water movement needed for thin, freely flowing mucus.
The established CF mechanism is defective CFTR-mediated epithelial salt/chloride and water transport, not altered skeletal-muscle Na+/K+-ATPase activity.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Rules out an unrelated muscle ion-pump mechanism.

evidence_map.claim: The patient's respiratory, digestive, sweat-chloride, and CFTR findings are explained by CFTR dysfunction and thick mucus rather than a lysosomal ganglioside-storage process.
CFTR dysfunction explains the patient's phenotype through abnormal salt/water transport and mucus formation; excessive intestinal iron absorption is not part of this mechanism.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Rules out an unrelated iron-regulatory mechanism.

evidence_map.claim: CFTR dysfunction causes the integrated pulmonary, pancreatic, and sweat phenotype; defective hepatic copper excretion does not account for these findings.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Rules out an unrelated copper-transport mechanism.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Reduced CFTR-mediated chloride transport disrupts coupled water movement and directly produces dehydrated, viscous airway secretions.
distractor_explanations.B: Incorrect. Skeletal-muscle Na+/K+-ATPase activity does not explain the epithelial chloride-transport defect, elevated sweat chloride, or thick airway mucus characteristic of cystic fibrosis.
distractor_explanations.C: Incorrect. Impaired lysosomal ganglioside degradation causes lysosomal storage disorders with prominent neurologic manifestations, not the CFTR-mediated pulmonary and pancreatic phenotype shown here.
distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect. Excess intestinal iron absorption causes systemic iron overload syndromes and does not produce the characteristic CFTR-related mucus abnormality.
distractor_explanations.E: Incorrect. Defective biliary copper excretion causes copper accumulation with hepatic and neurologic disease; it does not explain elevated sweat chloride or viscous airway secretions.

explanation.educational_objective: Cystic fibrosis results from pathogenic CFTR variants that impair epithelial chloride transport and water movement, producing thick, sticky secretions that obstruct airways and ducts.
explanation.key_explanation: The phenotype is cystic fibrosis. CFTR normally functions as an epithelial chloride channel and helps regulate salt and water movement across cell membranes. Pathogenic CFTR variants impair chloride transport and water movement, causing abnormally thick, sticky mucus in the airways and other ducts.

item.lead_in: Which of the following cellular abnormalities most directly contributes to the formation of thick airway secretions in this patient?

options.A: Decreased chloride transport across epithelial cell membranes
options.B: Increased sodium-potassium ATPase activity in skeletal muscle
options.D: Increased intestinal absorption of dietary iron
options.E: Defective hepatic excretion of copper into bile

item.tested_construct: CFTR loss of function impairs epithelial chloride transport and coupled water movement, dehydrating airway secretions.
item.vignette: A 7-year-old boy is evaluated for recurrent respiratory infections and poor weight gain. He has had several episodes of bacterial sinusitis and pneumonia. His stools are bulky and foul-smelling. Physical examination shows digital clubbing. Sweat chloride concentration is elevated, and genetic testing identifies pathogenic variants in CFTR.
